# EPUB Delivery

How a customer receives a purchased EPUB edition.

## Download Link

After payment clears, the shop emails a personal download link. The link is
valid for 48 hours and allows five downloads.

## Supported Readers

The shop ships DRM-free EPUB 3 files, which open in any EPUB reader app.

Identifier of one edition of a title, unique across the catalog.

## Retail Price (RP)

Price a customer pays for a title before discounts.

## Backorder

Order for a title that is out of stock, shipped when stock arrives.

name: bookshop/docs/ordering/checkout.md
src:
---
title: Checkout
---

# Checkout

How an order moves from the cart to payment.

## Payment Methods

The checkout accepts credit cards and gift cards. A gift card can cover part
of an order; the rest is charged to a card.

## Order Confirmation

The shop sends an order confirmation email with the order number and the
retail price of every title.

# EPUB download link after a resend

## Demand

Gifting an EPUB from a shared wishlist resends the download link to the
recipient; the SRD must say how long the resent link stays valid.

## Detail

The Download Link section states a 48-hour lifetime and five downloads for
the link sent after payment. It does not say whether a resend starts a new
48-hour window or reuses the original one. Support knows; not yet asked.

## Target claim

A resent download link is valid for 48 hours from the resend.

# SRD: Wishlist Sharing

A draft requirement for letting a reader share a wishlist by link. It is work
in progress, so the server reports no rank for it: an agent settling a
conflict trusts the published documentation and the knowledge base first.

## Requirements

- A reader can create a read-only link to one wishlist.
- Opening the link shows the titles without the reader's account details.

# Bookshop project configuration

Example `project-config.md` for a fictional online bookshop. Start the server
from it:

```shell
docket mcp -c examples/bookshop/project-config.md
```

The front matter holds flat keys only (text, number, checkbox, or list of
text), so Obsidian's Properties view can edit it. Every path is relative to
the project root, the directory holding this note; an absolute path, or one
escaping the root with `..`, stops the server. Keys the server does not use are
ignored, so the note can carry settings for other tools too. `kb` is read by
the companion SRD skills, not by the server.

A document's path is its location from the project root, for example
`docs/catalog/epub_delivery.md`; its identity is its front-matter `id` when
set (that document sets `epub-delivery`), else its path. The `.mcp.json`
beside this note registers `srd` on port 7777; the server refuses to
start when the two disagree.

`precedence` ranks the folders by trust, most trusted first, and every
`search`, `get_doc`, and `list_docs` result carries the document's `rank`:
`kb/shipping_times.md` gets 1, `docs/catalog/epub_delivery.md` 3, and the
unlisted `docs/glossary` folder ranks last, 4. Documents under `initiatives`
are work in progress and carry no rank. Rank never reorders search results;
agents use it to settle conflicting statements.

`gaps` names the gap folder, `gap`, which holds one Markdown file per gap;
filled and wontfix gaps move into its `closed/` subfolder. The sample `gap-0001-epub-download-link-after-a-resend.md` is an open gap,
partly filled by the Download Link section of `epub-delivery`; edit it in
Obsidian and the server keeps your changes.
